sentences.text: This animal possessed one of the largest cranial crests of any vertebrate and held one of the largest known pterosaur skulls, measuring approximately 1.42 meters in total length.
Although the fossil record contains only the skull, scientists estimate the creature had a wingspan ranging from 4.2 to 4.5 meters.
Its jaws were toothless but featured sharp edges on both the upper and lower sections.
The original skull was unearthed in 1983 near Santana do Cariri within the Araripe Basin of northeastern Brazil.
This specimen was first mentioned in an Italian publication in 1984 and received a preliminary description in 1990 by Kellner and Campos.
In 2002, Alexander Kellner and Diogenes de Almeida Campos formally named the species Thalassodromeus sethi, designating the skull as the holotype.
Kellner proposed that the animal fed like a modern skimmer, dragging its lower jaw through the water while in flight.
Later studies, however, suggested that the anatomy of the jaw and neck made this specific feeding method unfeasible for such large pterosaurs due to excessive drag and high energy costs.
Thalassodromeus is grouped with Tupuxuara in the clade Thalassodromidae, a group placed either within Tapejaromorpha or Neoazhdarchia depending on the specific study.

A jaw tip was initially described in 2015 as a new genus, Banguela oberlii, interpreted as a dsungaripterid, but was later reclassified as T. oberlii within Thalassodromeus in 2018 and reaffirmed in 2025.
This large pterosaur lived in northeastern Brazil during the early Late Cretaceous, approximately between 122 and 109 million years ago, specifically around 108 million years ago.
Fossils are found in the Romualdo Formation, where it shared its environment with other dinosaurs, pterosaurs, and animals.
Some scholars argue that the crest resembles the crown of the Egyptian god Amon rather than Seth.

A species named T. sebesensis was described in 2015 based on a crest fragment, but Dyke and colleagues later rejected this identification, arguing it was actually a fragment of the turtle Kallokibotion bajazidi.
